headline: Tightening freight market lifts Knight-Swift's earnings
summary_short: Revenue rose 12.6% y/y to $2.10B in Q2 FY2026 as a tightening truckload market lifted operating income 44.4% y/y to $104.9M and net income attributable to Knight-Swift 26.1% y/y to $43.2M ($0.26 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Truckload operating income rose $43.7M as a 5.5% gain in revenue per loaded mile outweighed a 2.6% drop in loaded miles; LTL added $3.3M on higher revenue per shipment; Intermodal added $4.1M on 19.6% higher load count. All Other Segments' operating income fell $17.2M on an $18.2M severance charge tied to the former executive chairman's retirement plus reclassified AR-securitization costs. Interest expense fell $17.6M on lower average debt and rates, but a $22.8M mark-to-market charge on U.S. Xpress earnout obligations widened other expense. For Q3 2026, management guides Truckload Adjusted Operating Ratio improving 650-750bp y/y and full-year net capex of $600-650M. Unrestricted cash was $186.1M; no shares were repurchased; the dividend held at $0.20/share.

drivers.explanation: The $8.9M increase in net income to $43.2M was driven by higher Truckload, LTL, and Intermodal operating income and lower interest expense, partially offset by a severance charge, an AR-securitization reclass, and a mark-to-market charge on U.S. Xpress earnout obligations.

Truckload revenue ex-fuel grew 2.8% y/y on a 5.5% gain in revenue per loaded mile; LTL revenue per shipment rose 3.4%; Intermodal load count rose 19.6%; Logistics revenue rose 8.9% on a 29.6% increase in revenue per load.

Not a company-reported line (no COGS/gross-profit caption in this carrier's income statement); this Yahoo-templated figure moved in step with the same freight-market pricing strength driving total revenue.

Segment operating income: Truckload +$43.7M on pricing gains, LTL +$3.3M, Intermodal +$4.1M; partly offset by All Other Segments -$17.2M on a severance charge and AR-securitization reclass, and Logistics -$1.7M on lower load count.
